bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "Greenhouse Gas Emissions Standards for Heavy-Duty Vehicles-Phase 3".
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution nullifies the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) rule titled Greenhouse Gas Emissions Standards for Heavy-Duty Vehicles—Phase 3 and published on April 22, 2024. Heavy-duty vehicles generally include vocational vehicles (such as public utility trucks and school buses) and tractors (such as cabs on tractor-trailer trucks). Among other requirements, the rule phases in standards to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from certain heavy-duty vehicles. The phased-in standards replace previous standards that were established under the EPA's Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Fuel Efficiency Standards for Medium- and Heavy-Duty Engines and Vehicles—Phase 2 rule with more stringent standards.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify an Environmental Protection Agency rule published in April 2024 that sets stricter greenhouse gas emission standards for heavy-duty vehicles such as delivery trucks, school buses, and tractor-trailers. The EPA rule phases in more stringent emission limits to replace earlier standards. If this resolution passes, the new stricter standards would be blocked and the previous, less stringent standards would remain in effect.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects regulatory obligations for operators of heavy-duty trucks, buses, and tractor-trailers subject to the emission standards.
The bill affects manufacturers of heavy-duty vehicles who must design and produce vehicles to meet the emission standards being nullified.
Stricter emission standards typically reduce fuel consumption in heavy-duty vehicles, affecting demand for diesel and other fossil fuels.
The emission standards may incentivize alternative fuel technologies and electrification of heavy-duty fleets, affecting clean-energy vehicle markets.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would cancel the EPA rule titled Greenhouse Gas Emissions Standards for Heavy-Duty Vehicles—Phase 3 and published on April 22, 2024.
plain.whoItTouches: People living near whatever is being regulated.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in the air, water and land where you live. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
